insights.core: NielsenIQ报告指出，智能家居升级已由‘智能’标签转向省钱、安全与去摩擦等实用价值，AI正渗透全屋并延伸至户外场景。58%消费者因降低水电费升级，四分之三翻新者考虑智能技术，49%会参考AI推荐。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，智能家居的购买逻辑与快消品趋同：消费者不为技术买单，而为可感知的利益买单。感官研究与消费者洞察应把‘省心、省钱、安全’转译为可测试的体验指标，并关注户外场景这一增量入口，避免陷入参数竞赛。
insights.action: 建议立即在消费者研究中加入‘利益感知’与‘AI推荐接受度’测试，覆盖室内外场景；同时跟踪水电账单节省、安防与户外烹饪等高频痛点，为产品概念与沟通提供可验证的决策依据。

insights.title: The Rise of the Home Barista: How Australia’s Coffee Machine Market Is Evolving Beyond Convenience Australia has long been regarded as one of the world's most sophisticated coffee markets. For decades, the café has been at the centre of the Australian coffee ritual, serving not just as a place to purchase a beverage, but as a cultural institution. Today, however, that ritual is increasingly extending into the home. The coffee machine category is undergoing a transformation. No longer viewed as a purely functional kitchen appliance, the modern coffee machine has become a lifestyle investment, a statement of personal taste, and, for many Australians, the gateway to recreating premium café experiences at home. NIQ's latest Purchase Insights+ Coffee Machine research reveals a market at an inflection point. While consumers remain highly value-conscious, they are simultaneously seeking elevated experiences, personalised solutions, and greater control over their daily coffee rituals. The result is a category that's evolving beyond convenience and moving firmly into the realm of lifestyle and aspiration. What emerges is a picture of a consumer who isn't simply buying a machine. They're investing in an experience. The Home Barista Revolution Has Arrived Historically, coffee machine purchases were driven primarily by replacement needs. While replacement remains the single largest trigger, accounting for 46% of purchases, the category is increasingly fuelled by consumers looking to improve their coffee experience rather than simply restore it. Nearly half of recent buyers entered the market either as first-time coffee machine owners (25%) or as consumers seeking an upgrade (22%). This shift signals an important evolution in consumer mindset. Coffee machines are becoming aspirational purchases. Among those upgrading, the motivations are particularly revealing. Consumers are seeking machines that better align with their coffee preferences, deliver authentic café-style coffee at home, offer greater functionality, and complement modern kitchen aesthetics. In many ways, the coffee machine has followed a similar path to categories such as premium televisions, smart home devices, and outdoor cooking equipment. What was once a utilitarian purchase is increasingly becoming a passion category. For brands, this represents a significant opportunity. The strongest growth is likely to come not from selling appliances, but from helping consumers become baristas in their own homes. Today's Coffee Shopper Is Highly Informed The purchase journey for coffee machines is remarkably considered. NIQ research shows that nine in ten buyers undertake some form of pre-purchase research, making coffee machines one of the more researched appliance categories. Consumers are not making impulse decisions. Instead, they're engaging in active comparison, evaluation, and education before committing to a purchase. Online browsing sits at the centre of this journey. Nearly half of consumers are exposed to digital information prior to purchase, and many spend days or even weeks researching before making a final decision. What are they looking for? Price remains influential, but consumers are equally focused on understanding functionality, comparing features, reading reviews, and evaluating different models and brands. They want confidence that they're choosing the right machine for their lifestyle, budget, and coffee preferences. This has major implications for manufacturers and retailers alike. Traditional product marketing is no longer enough. Consumers increasingly expect brands to educate them. Detailed product information, comparison tools, demonstration videos, authentic reviews, and helpful content have become essential parts of the purchase ecosystem. Increasingly, the brands that win are the brands that teach. Value Matters, But So Does Premiumisation One of the most intriguing findings from the research is the coexistence of value-conscious shopping behaviour and premium aspirations. On one hand, Australian consumers remain pragmatic. Cost and value are still the dominant drivers of purchase decisions, with competitive pricing, affordability, and overall value for money continuing to play a critical role. On the other hand, consumers are simultaneously pursuing higher quality products, trusted brands, premium experiences, and innovative features. This apparent contradiction is becoming increasingly common across consumer categories. Consumers may be feeling budget pressure, but that does not mean they are seeking the cheapest option available. Instead, they are looking for purchases that feel worthwhile. In an environment where discretionary spending decisions receive greater scrutiny, consumers want products that justify their investment. This dynamic becomes even more pronounced among buyers of fully automatic coffee machines, where quality emerges as a significantly stronger driver of choice. The implication for brands is clear: premiumisation remains a growth opportunity, but brands must articulate value alongside quality. Consumers are willing to spend more, provided they understand why the additional investment matters. The winning proposition is not premium alone. It is premium with purpose. Retail's Role Is Shifting From Distribution to Confidence Building Despite the digitalisation of the purchase journey, the store remains highly influential. Almost two-thirds of coffee machines are still purchased in-store, demonstrating that physical retail continues to play a vital role in the category. However, what consumers seek from retailers is evolving. Traditionally, retailers were valued for access and distribution. Today, they are equally valued for reassurance. Consumers gravitate towards retailers that offer competitive pricing, trusted environments, product variety, strong stock availability, and access to reputable brands. At the same time, digital channels are becoming indispensable sources of information and validation. The most effective purchase journeys now combine the strengths of both worlds. In physical stores, promotions, displays, product demonstrations, and knowledgeable staff help build confidence. Online, consumers rely on detailed specifications, product videos, reviews, retailer websites, and exclusive offers to narrow down their options. The future of coffee machine retail is therefore not a battle between online and in-store. It is a race to create the most seamless omnichannel experience. Coffee Machines Have Become Lifestyle Purchases Perhaps the most profound shift taking place within the category is emotional. Historically, appliance purchases have been driven largely by functionality. Consumers bought products to solve practical problems. While function remains important, coffee machines are becoming something more. The category increasingly intersects with identity, self-expression, and ritual. Consumers are drawn to products that reflect their personal coffee preferences, enhance their daily routines, and help recreate the experiences they enjoy outside the home. Design, aesthetics, coffee quality, and ease of use all contribute to the emotional appeal of the category. Notably, the single largest individual reason for purchase is that a machine "meets my needs." On the surface, this may sound functional. In reality, it reflects something deeper: consumers are looking for products that fit seamlessly into their lifestyle and support the experience they want to create. For many Australians, making coffee is no longer simply part of a morning routine. It has become a hobby, a ritual, and a daily moment of indulgence. The brands that understand this emotional dimension will be significantly better positioned for future growth. What This Means for the Industry What This Means for the Industry  As the category enters its next phase of growth, three consumer needs stand out.  Personalisation Consumers increasingly expect products tailored to their preferences, habits, and lifestyle. The ability to customise coffee experiences is becoming a competitive advantage. Premium Experiences Café-quality coffee at home is no longer a niche aspiration. It is becoming a mainstream expectation, creating opportunities for brands that can deliver quality, authenticity, and convenience simultaneously. Confidence Consumers want reassurance throughout the purchase journey. Rich educational content, trusted reviews, product demonstrations, and credible retail environments all help reduce uncertainty and strengthen conversion. The Bottom Line Australia's coffee machine market is no longer simply an appliance category. It sits at the intersection of coffee culture, consumer aspiration, and lifestyle enhancement. The next wave of growth will not be won by brands offering only superior technology or lower prices. It will belong to those that deliver premium experiences, build confidence throughout the purchase journey, and help consumers participate in the growing home barista movement. For manufacturers, retailers, and industry stakeholders, the opportunity is substantial. The battleground is no longer the appliance aisle. It is the morning ritual. Source: NIQ Purchase Insights+ Coffee Machine Study 2025, Australia (n=304 recent purchasers).  Purchase Insights+ Get inside the mind of your consumers. insights.title: August heatwaves scorch On-Premise drinks sales  Average sales in managed venues in the week to Saturday 15 August fell by 3.7% from the same week in 2025. That was followed by a year-on-year dip of 0.3% in the next seven days to Saturday 22 August. Adding in inflation makes these steeper drops in real terms. The latest figures mean that year-on-year sales fell for five straight weeks after the end of the football World Cup in mid-July. Very high temperatures in August prompted some consumers to stay close to home or switch their pub and bar visits to other open-air destinations. Footfall may also have been impacted by the splurge in spending during the World Cup, which led many fans to tighten their outgoings in the weeks afterwards. The Tracker, powered by CGA intelligence, shows daily sales were down particularly sharply during the middle few days of August, when temperatures peaked. However, trading picked up towards the end of the heatwaves, with year-on-year sales up on four of the six days between Monday 17 and Saturday 22 August.  The weather impacted most major categories, with cider the only one to grow sales (by 2.6% and 0.7% over the two weeks) as consumers sought refreshment from long cold serves. Beer (down 5.2% and up 1.5%) was slightly weaker. Soft drinks (down 0.9% and up 4.0%) had a mixed fortnight. It was another challenging period for spirits (down 17.4% and 11.6%) and wine (down 11.9% and 2.2%). Rachel Weller, NIQ’s commercial lead, UK & Ireland, said: “Warm weather is usually good news for pubs, bars and drinks suppliers, but recent heatwaves may have been too much for some consumers. Venues without outdoor spaces will have found it hardest to attract guests, and the wine and spirits categories have been particularly affected by the shift towards longer serves. Consumers’ economic uncertainty has added further to the challenges for the On-Premise over the summer. Respite from the heat will hopefully bring better footfall, but real-terms growth is likely to remain difficult for many.” The Daily Drinks Tracker provides analysis of sales at managed licensed premises across Britain and is part of NIQ's On-Premise suite of research services delivering in-depth data on category, supplier and brand rate of sale performance. insights.view: 对CMI而言，极端天气正成为即饮渠道独立于经济周期的扰动变量，且品类分化明显：长饮/冰饮场景受益，烈酒与葡萄酒受挤压。感官研究需关注高温下的适饮性与冰镇体验，渠道洞察需按门店有无户外空间分层，避免用总量数据掩盖结构性机会。
insights.action: 建议按天气与场景切分销售数据，重点监测无户外空间门店的客流流失；针对苹果酒、长饮及冰镇软饮开发高温限定饮用方案与陈列；对烈酒、葡萄酒测试清爽化产品与即饮调饮形态，并对冲经济不确定性下的消费降级。

insights.title: BEYOND REGULATION: HOW NEW CROSS-BORDER E-COMMERCE MEASURES ARE AFFECTING EUROPEAN CONSUMERS  Report Beyond Regulation: How New Cross-Border E-Commerce Measures Are Affecting European Consumers Download the report Resources Select the resources you would like to download. 2026 EU Tariffs Sentiment & Impact Study Over the past five years, cross-border e-commerce has grown rapidly across Europe, becoming an increasingly important source of products and value for consumers. However, the regulatory environment has recently begun to evolve, with new €3 flat tariffs, upcoming €2 handling fees, compliance requirements and other regulatory measures prompting platforms and merchants to adjust their business models and operations. Against this backdrop, NIQ conducted an online survey of 2,501 consumers across five key European markets — Germany, France, Italy, Spain and Poland — to understand how these changes are being experienced by consumers in their everyday shopping journeys. The study explores the tangible impact of the evolving cross-border e-commerce environment on consumer prices, product availability, choice and purchasing behavior. Amid a Broader Rise in Living Costs, New Tariffs on Cross-Border E-Commerce Add Further Pressure Around 87% of European consumers see cross-border e-commerce as an important channel for accessing affordable products, helping them better cope with rising prices. Since the introduction of new tariffs, European consumers’ monthly living expenses have increased by around 23%. Lower-income households have been more heavily affected. To cope with rising spending on cross-border e-commerce, lower-income households are cutting back on essential expenses, with clothing and footwear (53.6%), food (50.3%) and healthcare (19.5%) among the areas most affected. Fewer Categories, Fewer Choices, Slower Innovation — European Shoppers Are Feeling the Impact, While Local Migration Remains Limited 56% of consumers noticed reduced product category availability, while 40% ended up purchasing products that did not fully meet their needs as a result of reduced choice. Meanwhile, 26% perceived a slowdown in the introduction of new products. These shifts led consumers to spend 23% more time comparing and selecting products, on average. Among lower-income consumers, 67% reported a decline in their spending intentions, indicating a tangible impact on consumer behavior. Only 8% of consumers would shift their purchases to local e-commerce platforms or physical stores. The variety, convenience and affordability offered by cross-border e-commerce make it difficult for local channels to fully match its appeal. Consumers Generally Dissatisfied with Current Flat Duties on Cross-Border Purchases and Opposed to Further Increases 51% of European consumers are dissatisfied (rating 1–2 out of 5) with the additional duties or fees currently applied to cross-border purchases. More than 55% of European consumers would be dissatisfied with further increases in additional fees on cross-border e-commerce, in the context of the EU’s planned increase in handling fees for small parcels in November 2026. In the future Data indicates that the current regulatory trajectory is simultaneously causing a marked rise in the cost of living for low-income demographics and accelerating demand suppression, instead of redirecting it to local channels George Wang Consulting & Analytics, Business Lead, NIQ " As European consumers continue to rely on cross-border e-commerce for value, choice and access, policymakers and industry stakeholders should work together to better understand these unintended consumer impacts and ensure that regulatory changes do not disproportionately burden those who rely on these channels most constructive dialogues and communication among policymakers, platforms, merchants and consumers will be essential to finding a balanced path forward: One that protects consumers’ legitimate rights while preserving affordability, choice and access to innovation.” September 10 2026

insights.title: Why the Future of Marketing Effectiveness Belongs to AI-Native Decision Systems Why the Future of Marketing Effectiveness Belongs to AI-Native Decision Systems By Lauren Fernandes, Vice President of Global Content, NIQ Marketing leaders are under more pressure than ever to prove impact. At the same time, the pace of decision-making has accelerated beyond what traditional measurement workflows were designed to support. This shift calls for a new framework, one that helps businesses move from hindsight-based reporting to continuous, intelligence-driven decision-making. Marketing Has Reached an Operating-System Moment For years, the industry has responded to complexity by adding more dashboards, more reports, and more point solutions. Yet many organizations still struggle to answer the most important question: What should we do next, right now? The challenge isn't a lack of data. It's a lack of connected intelligence. As media buying becomes increasingly algorithmic and consumer journeys continue to fragment across retail, social, streaming, search, e-commerce, and in-store environments, the gap between insight generation and business action has become one of the defining challenges of modern marketing. "74% of CMOs said they were under more scrutiny for reporting marketing ROI, while only 9% believed they had unlocked real-time insights," says Tate. "So we have a 65-point gap between the pressure to answer questions and the ability to do so in real time." —Jason Tate, General Manager of Marketing Effectiveness at NIQ, describes this as the industry's growing "actionability gap." Beyond the Agent: The Rise of Coordinated Intelligence Much of the AI conversation has focused on the idea of a single, all-knowing assistant. The complex processes that marketing effectiveness solves cannot be facilitated by one single agent. Instead, it will be defined by networks of specialized intelligences working together across the measurement lifecycle. Think of it less as a chatbot and more as a high-performing, synchronized team. One agent cleans and harmonizes data. Another evaluates the models. Others surface insights, identify anomalies, benchmark performance, and recommend optimizations. Human marketers remain firmly in control, but they are supported by an ecosystem that can process information and surface decisions at machine speed. This shift represents something far more significant than automation. It is a redesign of the marketing effectiveness workflow itself. The old model was linear: collect data, run analysis, build reports, make decisions. The emerging model is always-on, continuously ingesting new signals, updating intelligence, and surfacing recommendations so that marketers and their AI systems can act on the most current information available. The organizations that embrace this transition will not simply gain efficiency. They will gain decision advantage. Introducing NIQ’s ‘Continuous Intelligence’ Framework As marketing enters the AI-native era, leaders need a new way to think about effectiveness. For decades, marketers relied on the Four P's of Marketing to shape growth strategy in a predictable, channel-centric world. Today's environment demands a different framework, one built not around products and promotions, but around intelligence and action. I call these the Drivers of Decision Velocity: five capabilities that move marketing effectiveness beyond measurement and into continuous, intelligence-led decision-making. Connect: Unify fragmented data sources into a trusted foundation. Contextualize: Understand performance within the realities of category, market, competitive, and consumer dynamics. Coordinate: Deploy specialized AI agents and analytics capabilities across measurement workflows. Commit: Translate insights into decisions while opportunities still exist. Compound: Capture organizational learning and continuously improve future recommendations. The power of this framework is that it transforms measurement from a reporting function into a decision engine. In other words, effectiveness no longer becomes something marketers review after campaigns conclude. It becomes something that actively guides performance while campaigns are running. The goal isn't better reporting. It's creating an engine for continuous decision-making and growth. Why Legacy Measurement Workflows Are Breaking Down Traditional measurement systems were built for a world with fewer channels, longer planning cycles, and relatively linear customer journeys. That world no longer exists. "Marketing leaders are being asked to do more with their budgets, prove business impact, and make decisions faster. It's not that legacy measurement workflows are bad; they were built for a different time." —Arica McKinnon, Global Head of Go-To-Market, Marketing Effectiveness at NIQ Today's challenge is not collecting data. It's reconciling thousands of fragmented signals that often tell conflicting stories. Measurement providers, media platforms, retail media networks, attribution tools, and internal systems all produce their own versions of performance. The result is often an organization filled with dashboards but lacking a common understanding of what is truly driving growth. The consequence is delayed action, slower optimization, and reduced confidence in decision-making. From Reports to Operating Rhythms Forward-looking organizations are beginning to recognize that they do not need another measurement tool. They need a new operating rhythm. One-time studies increasingly resemble historical snapshots. Valuable, but limited. Continuous decision systems, by contrast, are designed to keep pace with modern marketing. They allow marketers to move from reactive reporting toward proactive optimization. This is where AI-native platforms like NIQ Cadence™ point toward the future. Rather than layering AI onto legacy workflows, Cadence was built as a compound AI operating system, orchestrating specialized agents across data ingestion, harmonization, measurement, insights generation, and optimization. This distinction is important: The value is not simply that tasks happen faster. The value is that intelligence flows continuously across the workflow, enabling organizations to move from asking, "What happened?" to "What's happening, and what should we do next?" The Competitive Advantage of Continuous Decision-Making Over the next five years, the competitive divide in marketing will be determined by two factors: the depth of intelligence available to an organization and its ability to convert that intelligence into action at the speed of the market. Marketing effectiveness is evolving from a retrospective discipline into a real-time capability. The future will not belong to brands with the most reports. It will belong to those with the most adaptive decision systems. And as the industry moves beyond standalone AI agents toward coordinated intelligence ecosystems, platforms like NIQ Cadence offer a glimpse into what that future can look like: measurement that learns, evolves, and moves at the speed of modern marketing. By 2030, we may look back on static reporting much like the way we look back on batch data processing today: a necessary step in the industry's evolution, but no longer sufficient for how decisions get made. The next frontier is not more analytics. It's continuous intelligence. insights.action: 建议提前注册该研讨会，关注其趋势框架与数据来源；会后组织CMI与感官团队复盘，将'成功'议题映射到自身品类，检视现有消费者画像与产品叙事是否需迭代。

insights.title: The Ipsos Care-o-Meter: What does America know about vs. what does America care about?
insights.core: Ipsos提出Care-o-Meter框架，区分美国公众对议题的认知度与关心程度，揭示知晓不等于在乎，用于评估社会议题的真实优先级与传播潜力。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这提示消费者对产品、成分、健康议题的知晓度与购买驱动力常不匹配。仅凭认知度调研易高估卖点价值，需叠加关心度与行为意愿，才能识别真正影响决策的感官与健康诉求。
insights.action: 在感官与概念测试中同时测量知晓度与关心度，建立二维矩阵，筛出高关心低知晓的机会点，优先投入产品沟通与概念开发。

insights.title: Why Lowe’s CMO Jen Wilson added digital commerce to her portfolio
insights.core: Lowe's 首席营销官 Jen Wilson 将数字商务纳入其职责范围，反映零售企业正把电商运营与品牌营销整合到同一领导体系下，以打通消费者触达与转化的链路。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，这意味着渠道边界进一步模糊：线上货架、内容与转化数据将更紧密地并入营销决策。感官与消费者洞察需同步适配数字货架场景，如主图、短视频与评论对感官预期的塑造，而非仅依赖线下测试。
insights.action: 建议将数字商务指标纳入CMI研究框架，开展线上货架与内容对感官预期影响的专项测试，并与电商团队建立联合复盘机制，用转化与评价数据反哺产品感官优化。

insights.title: Jersey Mike’s kicks off NFL campaign as digital marketing spend surges
insights.core: Jersey Mike’s 借 NFL 赛季启动品牌营销，同步大幅增加数字营销预算，反映快消餐饮品牌正将资源向数字化渠道倾斜，以赛事赞助撬动流量。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，数字投放激增意味着消费者触点从传统媒体转向社交与程序化平台，感官与品牌体验需在碎片化内容中快速传递；赛事场景下的即时互动数据，可反哺口味偏好与消费场景洞察。
insights.action: 建议建立数字campaign实时监测看板，抓取赛事期间用户评论与UGC，关联感官关键词，快速迭代内容与产品沟通策略。

insights.title: How Carter’s is refreshing its brand to reach Gen Z, millennial parents
insights.core: Carter’s（美国童装品牌）正通过品牌焕新，以吸引Z世代和千禧一代父母，涉及视觉、传播与产品定位的年轻化调整。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，童装虽非食品，但同属家庭消费决策，其代际更替逻辑可迁移：感官线索（色彩、材质、包装）需匹配年轻父母对‘安全、审美、社交表达’的复合诉求。品牌焕新不能只靠口号，需建立代际偏好追踪机制。
insights.action: 建议在消费者研究中加入代际细分，测试新视觉与信息对Z世代/千禧父母的情感唤起与购买意愿，并定期监测品牌资产指标变化。

insights.title: NexChapter adds 2 executives to strengthen retail media and industry partnerships
insights.summary: Jeanie Hornung joins as principal and vice president of industry relationships while Ryan Colling takes on retail media manager role at convenience and grocery
insights.core: NexChapter 增设两名高管，Jeanie Hornung 任行业关系负责人，Ryan Colling 任零售媒体经理，重点强化便利店与杂货渠道的零售媒体及行业合作布局。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，零售媒体正成为连接消费洞察与购买转化的关键场域。这意味着感官偏好数据可与渠道媒体投放打通，在便利店与杂货场景中验证即时购买驱动，提升研究的商业落地性。
insights.action: 建议CMI团队主动对接零售媒体伙伴，将感官测试结果转化为可投放的渠道内容素材，优先在便利店与杂货场景试点，建立从偏好到购买的闭环度量。

insights.title: Food Lion to open six stores in Carolinas, Georgia by year’s end
insights.summary: First three stores will open in coming weeks in North Carolina and Georgia
insights.core: Food Lion宣布年底前将在卡罗来纳地区及佐治亚州新开六家门店，其中前三家未来几周内落地北卡与佐治亚，属区域性商超的持续扩张。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这意味着东南部区域零售覆盖密度上升，货架竞争与选品窗口同步扩大；区域连锁扩张常伴随自有品牌与本地化口味测试需求，是观察区域口味偏好与价格带迁移的天然实验场。
insights.action: 建议将该区域纳入零售审计与消费者测试样本框，跟踪新店品类结构与自有品牌动向；同步评估是否借新店开业窗口做产品铺货或感官偏好快测。

insights.title: Harps Food Stores Chairman and CEO to retire
insights.summary: Kim Eskew worked at the grocer since 1977 and will be replaced by grandson of founders
insights.core: 美国连锁超市Harps Food Stores宣布，自1977年任职至今的董事长兼CEO Kim Eskew即将退休，接任者为创始人的孙子，完成家族代际交接。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，家族企业代际交接往往伴随采购与自有品牌策略调整，新任领导者可能重新评估供应商合作与产品风味定位，是洞察渠道偏好变化的窗口期。
insights.action: 建议监测Harps新任CEO上任后的自有品牌与品类策略动向，评估其是否调整供应商结构，并提前准备针对区域超市渠道的感官差异化方案。

insights.title: Aldi is a growing threat to Walmart: analysis
insights.summary: About UsNewsletters AdvertiseWebinarsSubscribeSubscribeGrocery OperationsRelated TopicsGrocery TechnologyLegislation & Regulatory NewsMergers & AcquisitionsInde
insights.core: 该分析指出，Aldi凭借其精简SKU、高自有品牌占比和低价策略，正在美国杂货市场对Walmart构成日益增长的竞争威胁，反映出折扣零售渠道对主流大卖场的持续分流。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这意味着渠道结构变化将重塑消费者触点：Aldi自有品牌占比极高，品牌方需重新评估产品在折扣渠道的感官竞争力与包装沟通效率，同时消费者价格敏感度上升可能影响高端化叙事。
insights.action: 建议立即启动折扣渠道专项研究：对比Aldi与Walmart同品类自有品牌的感官表现与价格带，评估自身产品在精简货架下的被选概率，并调整CMI调研样本以覆盖折扣店购物者。

insights.title: Grocery Gauge: Some improvement in August
insights.summary: Earnings were a bit better and store visits held steady
insights.core: 8月杂货零售业绩略有改善，门店客流保持稳定，显示消费需求未进一步走弱但复苏力度有限。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，客流持稳意味着消费者仍在到店，但预算敏感度或延续，需关注性价比驱动下的产品体验与包装沟通。
insights.action: 建议在稳定客流中开展店内拦截测试，追踪价格敏感人群的感官偏好与购买动因，为Q4产品与促销策略提供依据。

insights.title: Target to open 8 stores in October
insights.core: Target计划在10月集中开设8家新门店，延续其实体扩张节奏。该信息来自零售行业媒体，反映大型零售商仍在通过线下网络布局强化市场覆盖与消费者触达。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，线下门店扩张意味着更多真实购买场景与货架接触点，可用于开展店内拦截测试、感官体验陈列及区域消费差异观察。Target客群偏中产家庭，其选品逻辑与自有品牌策略值得作为渠道洞察样本。
insights.action: 建议梳理Target新店所在区域的人口与消费画像，评估是否纳入下一轮门店拦截或产品试用测试点；同步关注其自有品牌上新动向，作为渠道选品与感官定位的参考。

insights.title: Old Navy’s new subbrand is a big bet on activewear
insights.core: Old Navy推出全新运动服饰子品牌，加码运动休闲赛道，反映其应对母品牌增长压力、抢占高增长品类的战略意图。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，运动休闲的竞争已从功能转向体感与情绪价值。面料触感、透气性、穿着舒适度等感官维度将成差异化关键，需前置布局运动场景下的消费者体感研究。
insights.action: 建议立即启动运动休闲品类的感官属性图谱与消费者穿着体验追踪，识别触感、透气、回弹等关键驱动因子，为产品开发与营销话术提供依据。

insights.title: Dueling Amazon, Target October sales events return
insights.core: 亚马逊与Target的十月大促同期回归，两大零售巨头再次正面交锋。此举延续了近年来十月打造新促销节点的趋势，意在提前锁定假日消费预算，争夺流量与市场份额。
insights.view: 对FMCG的CMI与感官研究而言，这意味着消费者决策窗口前移且更碎片化。十月大促将改变价格与促销敏感度的测量节奏，也要求感官与包装测试更贴近真实货架竞争环境，而非孤立评估。
insights.action: 建议提前布局十月前后的消费者追踪，监测跨渠道价格与促销反应；将感官/概念测试嵌入大促情境，评估在竞品夹击下的差异化表现，并据此调整Q4产品与沟通策略。

insights.title: DSW to test affordable luxury shop-in-shops
insights.core: DSW（美国鞋履零售商）计划测试‘平价奢侈品’店中店模式，在门店内引入高端品牌专区，以提升坪效与客流吸引力。摘要未提供具体品牌、时间或财务数据。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，店中店本质是‘场景化溢价’实验：需验证消费者在平价零售环境中对高端产品的感官预期是否被稀释，以及陈列、灯光、导购话术如何影响品质感知。这是零售环境对感官评价的干扰变量，值得纳入测试设计。
insights.action: 建议在类似店中店测试中，同步嵌入感官盲测与情境问卷，对比独立门店与店中店场景下的偏好、支付意愿与品质感知差异，建立‘环境溢价系数’参考，指导品类与陈列策略。

insights.title: Why Bonobos’ fall campaign centers on episodic content with Jack Quaid
insights.core: Bonobos 秋季营销以 Jack Quaid 主演的连续剧集式内容为核心，用分集叙事替代单次广告，拉长消费者接触周期并强化品牌角色代入感。
insights.view: 对CMI而言， episodic 内容把单次曝光转为多触点连续体验，品牌需以‘叙事一致性’衡量心智累积，而非仅看单集转化；感官与情绪线索应贯穿各集以维持记忆锚点，这要求研究从单点测试转向纵向追踪。
insights.action: 建议搭建分集内容的心智与情绪追踪机制，按周采集品牌联想、角色好感与购买意向，并同步测试不同感官线索在叙事中的记忆留存差异。

insights.title: The last mile of a food safety recall: It is not complete until consumers are protected
insights.summary: { document.querySelector('[data-progress-bar]').setAttribute('value',getScrollPercent()) })" @scroll.window="document.querySelector('[data-progress-bar]').setAt
insights.core: 文章指出食品安全召回不能止于产品下架，真正的‘最后一公里’是确保消费者实际收到并理解召回信息，从而避免风险。当前召回有效性评估常忽视消费者行为与沟通触达。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，召回沟通是消费者信任与品牌韧性的关键触点。感官研究可辅助识别异常批次，但召回有效性依赖消费者信息触达与行为响应。需将召回沟通纳入消费者洞察体系，评估不同渠道与信息设计对消费者认知和行动的影响。
insights.action: 建立召回沟通的消费者触达与行为监测机制，测试召回信息在包装、短信、社媒等渠道的清晰度与行动转化，并纳入危机管理演练。

insights.title: EU proposes changes to rules about meat storage conditions
insights.summary: The European Commission has opened a comment period on a change to regulations that would give companies more flexibility related to frozen meat.The proposals w
insights.core: 欧盟委员会就冷冻肉储存条件规则修订开放意见征询，拟赋予企业更大灵活性，允许在合规框架下调整冷冻肉储存方式，以降低合规成本并提升供应链效率。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，储存条件松绑可能改变肉类产品的质构、色泽与风味释放曲线，进而影响消费者接受度。需警惕感官品质波动带来的品牌感知风险，同时为产品差异化提供新空间。
insights.action: 立即跟踪法规文本与意见截止日，评估自有肉类/预制菜产品在冷冻储存变更下的感官稳定性，并启动消费者盲测，验证质构与风味变化是否在可接受阈值内。

insights.title: Sri Lanka creates food safety policy with FAO support
insights.summary: Sri Lanka has unveiled its first national food safety policy with six themes including improving food controls, strengthening surveillance, and enhancing standa
insights.core: 斯里兰卡在联合国粮农组织支持下发布首个国家食品安全政策，涵盖改善食品管控、强化监测、提升标准等六大主题，旨在构建系统性食品安全治理框架。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这意味着斯里兰卡市场准入门槛与合规要求将趋严，产品感官标准、标签与质量一致性需对接新规；同时监管升级可能改变消费者对本地食品安全的信任与偏好，为跨国品牌创造差异化机会。
insights.action: 建议立即梳理斯里兰卡现行法规与新政差异，评估产品配方、感官指标及供应链合规风险；同步启动当地消费者食品安全认知与信任度调研，为进入或调整市场策略提供依据。

insights.title: Abbott to pay almost $385 million to settle false claims allegation about infant formula
insights.summary: The settlement resolves a case by the federal government related to allegations about false claims and is not a determination of liability on the part of the co
insights.core: 雅培因婴儿配方奶粉虚假声明指控，同意支付近3.85亿美元与美国联邦政府和解，该和解不构成对其责任的认定。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这提示配方宣称的合规风险正被放大。感官与消费者研究若支撑‘接近母乳’等主张，必须确保数据可验证、口径一致，否则易被监管或诉讼挑战。
insights.action: 立即审查现有配方宣称的感官与消费者证据链，建立宣称-数据映射表，并让CMI与法务提前介入新品宣称设计。

insights.title: Smelling chocolate helped men complete more reps without feeling more tired
insights.summary: Simply smelling chocolate helped men complete more leg extension repetitions without making the workout feel harder, with dark chocolate producing the strongest
insights.core: 研究发现，仅闻巧克力气味即可让男性完成更多腿部伸展重复次数，且不增加主观疲劳感，其中黑巧克力气味效果最强。这提示嗅觉刺激可影响运动表现与疲劳感知。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究而言，嗅觉线索不仅关乎愉悦与购买，还可能调节生理表现与努力感知。这为能量/运动营养、功能食品及电子雾化产品的气味设计提供了新卖点：通过特定香韵降低努力感、提升表现，值得纳入CMI测试。
insights.action: 建议在感官实验室复现该实验，量化不同巧克力香韵对运动耐力与RPE的影响，并测试其在能量胶、蛋白粉或雾化产品中的可迁移性，评估作为差异化宣称的可行性。

insights.title: NAPCOR envisions cutting PET bottle life-cycle emissions 57% by 2050
insights.core: NAPCOR公司提出到2050年将PET瓶全生命周期排放削减57%的目标，聚焦包装材料的可持续转型与碳足迹管理。
insights.view: 对快消品CMI而言，包装可持续性正成为消费者感知与品牌偏好的新维度。感官研究需关注包装触感、开启声等体验是否因轻量化或再生材料改变，进而影响产品整体感知。
insights.action: 建议在消费者测试中纳入包装可持续性认知与感官体验的关联评估，追踪再生PET对产品品质感知的潜在影响，为包装创新提供洞察支持。

insights.title: Passing the sniff test: Overcoming PCR’s odor and color challenges
insights.summary: Sensory issues related to scent and tint pose unique hurdles for brands looking to incorporate more recycled plastic in consumer goods packaging. It’s
insights.core: 包装行业在提升消费后回收塑料（PCR）使用比例时，遭遇气味与色泽两大感官障碍，影响品牌采用意愿。文章探讨了这些挑战的成因及应对思路。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，包装已非单纯视觉议题，而是多感官体验触点。回收料气味可能迁移至内容物或形成负面嗅觉联想，色泽波动则冲击货架一致性与品质感知，需将包装感官纳入消费者测试体系。
insights.action: 建议在包装变更前开展盲测与使用情境测试，量化气味、色泽对感知与购买意向的影响；同步与供应商设定感官阈值标准，建立回收料批次感官筛查流程。

insights.title: Coca-Cola to spend $10B on US manufacturing by 2030
insights.core: 可口可乐宣布到2030年在美国制造业投入100亿美元，用于扩大本土生产与供应链布局。该投资反映其在关税与成本压力下强化本地化产能、贴近市场的战略取向。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，本土产能扩张意味着配方微调、原料来源变化与新品上市节奏加快，需前置评估其对口味一致性与感官体验的潜在影响，并同步追踪消费者对‘美国制造’标签的感知与溢价接受度。
insights.action: 建议将本土生产变更纳入感官差异测试与消费者追踪计划，建立产线切换的口味基准库；同时开展‘本土制造’主张的CMI验证，明确其对购买意愿与品牌信任的实际拉动。

insights.title: Mars zeroes in on gut health with startup partnerships
insights.core: Mars（玛氏）通过投资肠道健康领域初创企业来布局功能性食品赛道，反映出大型快消巨头正将肠道健康视为下一个产品创新与消费者沟通的核心战场。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，肠道健康产品的挑战在于功效成分往往带来不良风味与口感，感官团队需提前介入配方与掩味技术评估；同时消费者对'肠道健康'的认知与支付意愿需通过定性研究厘清，避免概念自嗨。
insights.action: 建议立即启动两项工作：一是梳理自身品类与肠道健康成分的适配机会点；二是开展消费者定性访谈，明确目标人群对肠道健康功效的信任来源、风味容忍度及溢价接受区间。

insights.title: Nestlé ‘not happy’ with food giant’s performance in North America
insights.core: 雀巢管理层对公司在北美市场的业绩表现明确表达不满，反映这家食品巨头在其最大区域市场正面临增长乏力或份额承压的困境，具体原因未在摘要中披露。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，这是典型的成熟市场增长警报：北美消费者偏好快速向健康化、功能化、性价比迁移，传统大品牌若感官体验与价值主张未同步迭代，易被新兴品牌蚕食。感官研究需重新校准本地口味图谱与质地偏好，验证产品线是否仍匹配主流需求。
insights.action: 立即启动北美核心品类的感官与消费者追踪，定位体验短板与流失人群；结合竞品拆解输出产品改良与沟通优先级，向管理层提供可落地的区域复兴假设清单。

insights.title: Mondelēz set to relaunch ‘star brand’ Oreo in 2027
insights.core: 亿滋国际计划于2027年重新推出其明星品牌奥利奥，但摘要仅含图片链接，未披露具体产品、市场或营销策略细节。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，品牌重启需前置验证配方、口感与包装的消费者接受度。奥利奥作为成熟资产，重启可能涉及健康化、本土化或高端化方向，感官属性与情感联结的平衡是关键。
insights.action: 建议立即启动奥利奥现有消费者心智与竞品感官基准研究，追踪健康趋势与口味偏好，为2027年重启储备概念与产品测试数据。

insights.title: Lion adds two Kirin Hyoketsu flavours to Australia’s RTD market
insights.summary: Both innovations are made with vodka, soda and natural fruit juice using Kirin’s signature Hyoten Toketsu method. The post Lion adds two Kirin Hyoketsu flavours
insights.core: Lion将麒麟Hyoketsu两款新口味引入澳大利亚RTD市场，产品以伏特加、苏打水和天然果汁为基础，采用麒麟标志性‘冰点冻结’工艺，强调果味与冰爽口感。
insights.view: 对感官研究而言，RTD竞争正从风味数量转向工艺叙事带来的差异化口感。‘冰点冻结’可能影响冰爽感、果香释放与甜酸平衡，是感官属性与消费者感知的联结点，值得在CMI中拆解为可测量的感官维度。
insights.action: 建议针对该工艺建立感官描述词库，对比竞品在冰爽感、果香真实度、余味干净度上的差异，并通过消费者测试验证工艺故事能否转化为可感知的体验优势。

insights.title: FamilyMart taps AI to develop new sweets
insights.summary: The first commercial result of this process is a sweet potato canele with caramel sauce, priced at $2.58. The post FamilyMart taps AI to develop new sweets appe
insights.core: 全家便利店利用AI开发新品甜点，首款商业化产品为焦糖酱红薯可露丽，售价2.58美元，标志AI正式介入快消品口味研发与商品化流程。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，AI正从数据分析工具转向配方共创角色，可加速概念筛选与风味组合，但消费者接受度、感官描述与情感偏好仍需真人验证。便利店高频上新场景将成为AI感官预测的天然试验场。
insights.action: 建议建立AI生成概念与消费者感官测试的对照机制，追踪该产品复购与评价数据，评估AI配方在真实货架中的表现，并沉淀可复用的风味预测模型。

insights.title: What did Woolworths see in the IGA down the road?
insights.summary: What one bizarre visit reveals about the serious power imbalance between independents and the majors. The post What did Woolworths see in the IGA down the road?
insights.core: 文章借一次探访独立零售商IGA的见闻，揭示澳洲连锁超市Woolworths与独立杂货商之间严重的权力失衡，反映大型零售商对供应链与渠道的强势掌控。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，渠道权力失衡意味着独立渠道的消费者数据与反馈更易被忽视；若品牌仅依赖大零售商样本，将错失独立渠道的品类偏好与价格敏感度差异，导致洞察偏差。
insights.action: 建议在CMI调研中纳入独立零售商与区域渠道样本，建立分渠道感官与购买行为对比；同时评估渠道议价力对产品定价、包装与铺货策略的影响。

insights.title: Arizona accuses L’Oréal of concealing cancer risks linked to hair relaxers
insights.summary: The state is seeking a court order forcing L’Oréal to stop selling the products unless it warns of the cancer risk. The post Arizona accuses L’Oréal of conceali
insights.core: 亚利桑那州指控欧莱雅隐瞒其直发产品与癌症风险的关联，并寻求法院强制其下架产品或加注警示。这是继多起诉讼后，监管与司法层面对美发产品安全性的又一次施压。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，产品安全正成为消费者信任与购买决策的核心变量，感官宣称（如顺滑、持久）若与健康风险挂钩，将迅速被负面舆情覆盖。需警惕成分安全议题向品类整体蔓延，影响消费者对品牌及渠道的信任。
insights.action: 立即排查在售直发/烫发类产品的成分合规与警示标识；建立安全舆情监测与快速响应机制；在CMI调研中增加成分安全与风险感知维度，评估对购买意愿的潜在冲击。

insights.title: Nestlé, Starbucks launch Refreshers Concentrates for at-home drinks
insights.summary: The product is made with green coffee extract and is available in three fruit flavors. The post Nestlé, Starbucks launch Refreshers Concentrates for at-home dri
insights.core: 雀巢与星巴克合作推出Refreshers浓缩液，含绿咖啡提取物，提供三种水果口味，定位居家自制饮品场景，将咖啡馆风味延伸至家庭消费。
insights.view: 居家饮品场景持续升温，浓缩液形态兼顾便捷与个性化调配。对感官研究而言，需关注绿咖啡提取物与水果风味的平衡及稀释后的风味衰减；对CMI而言，应追踪消费者自制习惯与口味偏好，验证场景迁移的接受度。
insights.action: 建议开展居家调配感官测试，评估不同稀释比例的风味表现；同步调研目标人群的自制饮品频率与口味需求，为后续口味迭代与场景营销提供依据。

insights.title: Coles adds K-beauty to its skincare category
insights.summary: The move comes as K-beauty continues to attract attention through social media, ingredient-led product discovery and demand for simple skincare routines. The po
insights.core: Coles 将 K-beauty 引入其护肤品类，反映韩国美妆正通过社交媒体传播、成分导向的产品发现方式以及消费者对精简护肤流程的需求，持续获得主流零售渠道的关注。
insights.view: 对 FMCG 感官与 CMI 而言，这标志着成分叙事与社媒种草正在重塑护肤购买路径。零售商自有渠道的引入意味着 K-beauty 从细分走向大众，感官体验（质地、吸收感、香气）需与成分宣称协同验证，消费者测试应覆盖精简流程下的真实使用场景。
insights.action: 建议立即开展 K-beauty 竞品货架审计与消费者感官偏好测试，重点评估质地、肤感与成分可信度；同时监测社媒成分话题趋势，为自有品牌或引进选品提供数据支撑。

insights.title: Abbott to pay US$384m to resolve claims over infant formula
insights.summary: The lawsuit followed a 2022 recall of Abbott baby formula products. The post Abbott to pay US$384m to resolve claims over infant formula appeared first on Insid
insights.core: 雅培因2022年婴儿配方奶粉召回事件引发的诉讼，将以3.84亿美元和解相关索赔。该事件涉及产品质量与安全争议，对品牌声誉和消费者信任造成持续影响。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此案警示产品安全危机可迅速升级为法律与财务风险。感官研究需强化早期预警，CMI应监测消费者信任度波动，尤其在母婴品类，安全感知直接驱动购买决策与品牌忠诚。
insights.action: 建议立即复盘自身产品召回与危机沟通机制，将感官质量指标纳入风险监测体系，并建立消费者信任度追踪，以降低类似事件对品牌资产的冲击。

insights.title: Energy & Natural ResourcesResilience, Refined: The New Downstream Oil and Gas Playbook Four capabilities worth at least $2 to $3 per barrel are separating the refiners that pull ahead.
insights.summary: Bookmark content that interests you and it will be saved here for you to read or share later.
insights.core: 贝恩指出，炼油企业通过四项关键能力可在每桶油上获得至少2至3美元的价值优势，从而在行业竞争中脱颖而出，核心在于以韧性为核心重塑下游油气业务模式。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这提示价值增量来自体系化能力而非单点优化。炼油业以每桶收益量化能力价值，启示我们应将感官与消费者洞察转化为可量化的商业杠杆，如溢价、复购与转化率，而非停留在描述性偏好。
insights.action: 建立感官与CMI能力的价值量化框架，将洞察指标与定价、复购等业务结果挂钩，识别并优先投入2至3项高杠杆能力，形成可复用的韧性研究体系。

insights.title: AI, Insights, and SolutionsThe Era of Experimentation Is Over with Arvind Krishna, CEO of IBMCEO Arvind Krishna joins Sarah and Andrew to discuss what the company has learned along the way—and how those lessons are shaping the IBM playbook.
insights.summary: Bookmark content that interests you and it will be saved here for you to read or share later.
insights.core: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna在贝恩访谈中复盘IBM的AI落地历程，指出AI实验期已结束，企业需从试点转向规模化部署，并提炼出可复制的打法。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，AI不再是概念验证，而是重构消费者洞察链路的生产力工具：文本挖掘、感官描述词聚类、跨市场趋势识别均可规模化。关键教训在于先明确业务问题再选模型，避免为技术而技术。
insights.action: 梳理现有感官与CMI流程中可被AI替代或增强的环节，选定1-2个高价值场景做规模化试点，并建立效果衡量指标，六个月内形成可复用模板。

insights.title: RetailPoul Weihrauch, Mars: Purpose Is Easy Until It’s Tested What does it take to build a business that can pass the purpose-driven test?
insights.summary: Bookmark content that interests you and it will be saved here for you to read or share later.
insights.core: Bain访谈Mars CEO Poul Weihrauch，探讨企业如何构建经得起考验的使命驱动型业务，强调使命在顺境中易谈、在压力下才见真章，核心是使命与商业决策的一致性。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，这是提醒：消费者对品牌使命的感知最终落在产品体验上。若可持续、健康等主张未在感官层面兑现，使命叙事会在真实选择中被证伪。研究需把使命转化为可测量的感官与体验指标。
insights.action: 在感官与消费者测试中引入使命一致性维度，检验产品体验是否支撑品牌主张；建立压力场景下的选择测试，观察价格、便利等权衡时使命的权重变化。

insights.title: Refurbished Smartphones: Australia’s Next Telecom Growth Engine Australia's smartphone market is undergoing a significant shift. New smartphone sales volumes declined 12% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, according to the NIQ Market Intelligence Sales Tracking Panel. At the same time, device prices continue to rise while consumers are holding onto their smartphones for longer, extending replacement cycles across the market. With fewer than half of Australians planning to upgrade within the next 12 months, based on a recent NIQ consumer study, traditional handset growth models are coming under increasing pressure. That pressure is landing on a consumer who is already trading down: 47% of Australians name inflation and high prices as one of their top three concerns — the single biggest worry in the market and well above the 34% global average — and 42% have switched from name brands to less expensive brands in the past year, based on NIQ Consumer Life Global 2026 study. Yet hidden within this challenge is a significant opportunity: refurbished smartphones. Consumer demand already exists. According to the same NIQ consumer study, more than one-third of Australians aged 18 and above who are considering a future smartphone upgrade say they would likely purchase a refurbished device. Interest is highest among consumers aged 18 to 44 and those planning to upgrade in the near term, highlighting growing consumer acceptance of refurbished smartphones as an affordable pathway to premium technology. While affordability drives interest in refurbished smartphones, trust remains the biggest barrier to adoption. Australians remain concerned about battery health, hidden defects, warranty protection, and refurbishment quality. Research shows that consideration increases significantly when refurbished devices are backed by a trusted mobile network operator that offers certified quality checks and warranty support. Top Consumer Concerns by Key Themes Top Consumer Concerns by Key Themes  72% - Quality & Performance 41% worry about battery life, followed by 38% fear hidden issues emerging later, and 33% are unsure how well the device was refurbished. 49% - Warranty/Risk Transparent warranty and returns protection can significantly reduce perceived risk and build consumer confidence.​ 39% - Value Trust, rather than price, remains the key adoption barrier. Consumers are more likely to respond to quality assurance and warranty protection than aggressive price reductions. 31% - Trust/Security Stronger trust signals around seller credibility, refurbishment standards, and certified data wiping can help alleviate consumer security concerns. Consumer Trends Are Creating the Right Conditions Australian consumer attitudes are increasingly aligned with refurbished smartphones. Inflation and high prices remain Australians' biggest concern (47%), driving more value conscious behaviours. Nearly 44% of Australians bought something second-hand instead of new in the past year — far above the 26% global average — while 48% postponed a purchase until the product was on sale and 42% switched from name brands to less expensive brands. Australians are also more likely than consumers globally to have cut back on nonessential spending (58% vs. 53%). Trust remains a key enabler of refurbished smartphone adoption NIQ Consumer Life research shows that value for money is the #2 most-held life attitude in Australia among 44 measured attitudes: 53% of Australians agree, “for me, the most important thing about a brand is that it offers good value for the money.” Price is the #5 attitude nationally (45% agree it is the most important factor in their purchasing decisions), versus #13 globally. Trust is the qualifier on that value equation rather than a rival to it — 31% of Australians say they only buy from a trusted brand, and 52% will simply choose an alternative if a product or service disappoints them, the #4 attitude in the market. This presents a clear opportunity for operators and certified refurbishers to build confidence through transparent grading, certified quality checks, and warranty-backed support. The long view: a decade of value and trust rising together This is not a post-inflation blip. Over twelve years of Consumer Life tracking in Australia, the two attitudes have risen together: demanding good value for money has climbed from 44% to 53%, and insisting on a trusted brand has climbed further, from 20% to 31%. Australians have not traded trust away in pursuit of a cheaper device — they have raised the bar on both at once. A refurbished handset sold without certified grading and warranty fails the second test even when it wins the first. The UK Provides a Glimpse Into Australia's Future If Australia wants to understand where the refurbished market could be heading, the UK offers a compelling blueprint. Refurbished smartphones have been part of the UK market for more than a decade. Today, refurbished devices account for nearly 1 in 10 smartphone sales volume in the UK. Refurbished smartphone sales are growing 14% year on year, significantly outperforming the new smartphone market, which declined 7% over the same period. The UK demonstrates that refurbished devices do not cannibalise new smartphone demand. In fact, they benefit from it. New flagship launches generate trade ins, increase the supply of premium refurbished devices, and create affordable upgrade opportunities for consumers who aspire to own premium brands but cannot justify the latest flagship price. A White Space Opportunity for Operators and Resellers The real opportunity extends beyond selling refurbished phones. Mobile Network Operators that can manage the entire device lifecycle, from financing and trade in to refurbishment, resale, protection, and upgrades, can unlock new revenue streams while improving customer retention. International markets are increasingly moving in this direction, treating devices as recurring assets rather than one-time transactions. Existing brand trust, customer relationships, retail footprints, and financing capabilities provide operators with a competitive advantage that many independent sellers cannot replicate. For specialist refurbishers, the opportunity lies in building trust through transparent grading, battery guarantees, certified testing, and robust warranty programmes. The Bottom Line Australia's refurbished smartphone market remains underdeveloped compared with more mature markets such as the UK. However, many of the conditions that fuelled growth overseas is already emerging locally: rising flagship prices, longer replacement cycles, growing acceptance of second hand purchases, and an increasing focus on value. The winners will be those who help shape the market, not wait for it to mature. Operators, retailers, and refurbishers that invest early in trusted refurbishment programs and device lifecycle strategies will be best positioned to capture future growth. Understand the consumers behind the trends Explore insights from the NIQ Consumer Life Study to uncover how shifting attitudes toward value, trust, and spending are reshaping market opportunities.
