readings.title: Let’s stop calling them “soft skills” — and call them “real skills” instead
body: Let’s stop calling them “soft skills” — and call them “real skills” instead
We persist in hiring and training as if we’re running a bowling squad, as if easily measured skills are all that matter.

What causes successful organizations to fail ? What makes stocks fade, innovations slow, customers jump ship? We can agree that certain skills are essential. That hiring coders who can’t code, salespeople who can’t sell, or architects who can’t design is a waste. But these skills — let’s call them vocational skills — have become the backbone of the recruitment process.

But how do you explain that similar organizations, with similarly vocationally skilled people, find themselves with very different outcomes? Most of the textbooks that students experience and the tests they take are about vocational skills, the checkboxes that have to be checked to get a job. By misdefining “vocational” and focusing on these allegedly essential skills, we’ve diminished the value of the other skills that matter.

We give too little respect to the other skills when we call them “soft” and imply that they’re optional. What actually separates thriving organizations from struggling ones are the difficult-to-measure attitudes, processes and perceptions of the people who do the work.

Vocational skills can be taught: You’re not born knowing engineering or copywriting or even graphic design, therefore they must be something we can teach. But we let ourselves off the hook when it comes to decision-making, eager participation, dancing with fear, speaking with authority, working in teams , seeing the truth, speaking the truth, inspiring others, doing more than we’re asked, caring and being willing to change things. We underinvest in this training, fearful that these things are innate and can’t be taught. Perhaps they’re talents. And so we downplay them, calling them soft skills, making it easy for us to move on to something seemingly more urgent.

At scale, organizations pay less attention to soft skills when hiring because we’ve persuaded ourselves that vocational skills are impersonal and easier to measure. If it’s easier to test for, it seems more important when selecting our team.
And we fire slowly (and retrain rarely) when these skills are missing, because we’re worried about stepping on toes, being called out for getting personal or possibly wasting time on a lost cause.

But these skills can all be learned, as obvious skills like chess or typing can be learned. We learn them accidentally, by osmosis, by the collisions we have with teachers, parents, bosses and the world. Even though they’re more difficult to measure, that doesn’t mean we can’t improve them, can’t practice them or can’t change the way we do our work.

Let’s stop calling them soft. They’re interpersonal skills. Leadership skills. The skills of charisma and diligence and contribution. But these modifiers, while accurate, somehow edge them away from the vocational skills, the skills that we actually hire for, the skills we measure a graduate degree on.
So let’s uncomfortably call them real skills instead.
Real because they work, because they’re at the heart of what we need today.
Real because even if you’ve got the vocational skills, you’re no help to us without these human skills, the things that we can’t write down or program a computer to do.
Real skills can’t replace vocational skills, of course. What they can do is amplify the things you’ve already been measuring.
Imagine a team member with all the traditional vocational skills: productive, skilled, experienced. A resume that can prove it. That’s a fine baseline.

Now add to it. Perceptive, charismatic, driven, focused, goal-setting, inspiring and motivated. Generous, empathic and consistent. A deep listener , with patience. What happens to your organization when someone like that joins your team?
Writing in the Harvard Business Review , Lou Solomon reports that 69 percent of managers are uncomfortable communicating with their employees. I’d guess that many of the other 31 percent are lying.

Communicating with employees is uncomfortable because we’ve built systems of compliance and dominance that make it difficult. We ask people to leave their humanity at the door, then use authority to change behavior. We overlay corporate greed and short-term thinking with a human desire to create work that matters.

How do we build people-centric organizations while also accepting the fact that two thirds of our managers (presumably well paid, well trained and integral to our success) are so uncomfortable doing an essential part of their job that they admitted it to a stranger?

In a recent survey, the Graduate Management Admission Council reported that although MBAs were strong in analytical aptitude, quantitative expertise and information-gathering ability, they were sorely lacking in other critical areas that employers find equally attractive: strategic thinking, written and oral communication, leadership and adaptability . Are these mutually exclusive? Must we trade one for the other?

The foundation of all real skills is this one: the confidence and permission to talk to one another. Not to manage, belittle, intimidate or control. Simply to seek to be understood and to do the work to understand.

##段落 让我们别再称它们为“软技能”——改叫“真实技能”吧
##段落 2023年6月9日
##段落 赛斯·高汀
##段落 脸书 X LinkedIn Reddit WhatsApp
##段落 黛博拉·什皮尔曼
##段落 我们招人和培训时，仍像在组建一支保龄球队，仿佛只有那些容易衡量的技能才重要。
##段落 是什么让成功的组织走向失败？是什么让股票失色、创新放缓、客户流失？我们都认同某些技能不可或缺。招进来却不会编程的程序员、不会销售的销售员，或不会设计的建筑师，都是浪费。但这些技能——姑且称之为职业技能——已成为招聘流程的支柱。
##段落 但你怎么解释，相似的机构、拥有职业技能相似的人，却得到截然不同的结果？学生接触的大多数教科书和参加的考试，都围绕职业技能，也就是求职时必须勾选的复选框。由于对“职业”的误定义，以及对所谓必备技能的过度聚焦，我们贬低了其他重要技能的价值。
##段落 当我们把其他技能称为“软”技能，暗示它们可有可无时，我们给了它们太少的尊重。真正区分蓬勃发展的组织与苦苦挣扎的组织，是那些从事工作的人的难以衡量的态度、流程和认知。
##段落 职业技能可以教授：你不是天生就懂工程、文案甚至平面设计，因此它们必然是可以传授的。但在决策、积极投入、与恐惧共舞、有权威地表达、团队协作、看清真相、说出真相、激励他人、做超出要求的事、关心他人并愿意改变现状等方面，我们却放任自己。我们对这类培训投入不足，担心这些东西是天生的、教不会。也许它们是天赋。于是我们轻视它们，称其为软技能，让自己轻易转向看似更紧迫的事。
##段落 在规模化层面，组织在招聘时对软技能关注更少，因为我们说服自己：职业技能更客观、更容易衡量。如果更容易测试，在挑选团队时就显得更重要。
##段落 而当这些技能缺失时，我们解雇得很慢（也很少再培训），因为我们担心得罪人、被指责针对个人，或可能在无望的事情上浪费时间。
##段落 但这些技能都可以学习，就像象棋或打字等显而易见的技能可以学习一样。我们是在无意中、通过潜移默化、通过与老师、父母、老板和世界的碰撞中学到的。尽管它们更难衡量，但这并不意味着我们不能改进它们，不能练习它们。

##段落
他们不能改变我们的工作方式。
##段落
当然可以。
##段落
让我们停止称它们为软技能。它们是人际交往能力。领导能力。魅力、勤奋和贡献的能力。但是这些修饰词虽然准确，却在某种程度上将它们与职业技能——我们实际招聘时所看重的技能、我们衡量研究生学位的技能——拉开了距离。
##段落
所以，让我们不无尴尬地称它们为“真实技能”吧。
##段落
真实，因为它们行之有效，因为它们是我们当今所需的核心能力。
##段落
真实，因为即使你拥有职业技能，如果没有这些人际能力——那些我们无法写下来、也无法编程让计算机去做的事情——你对我们而言也毫无用处。
##段落
真实技能当然不能取代职业技能。它们能做的是放大你已经在衡量的那些东西。
##段落
想象一位拥有所有传统职业技能的团队成员：高效、专业、经验丰富。一份能证明这一切的简历。这是一个不错的基本线。
##段落
现在在此基础上叠加：敏锐、有魅力、有驱动力、专注、善于设定目标、鼓舞人心且充满动力。慷慨、有同理心且始终如一。一个深度倾听者，富有耐心。当这样的人加入你的团队时，你的组织会发生什么？
##段落
卢·所罗门在《哈佛商业评论》中写道，69%的管理者与员工沟通时感到不自在。我猜另外31%中的许多人是在撒谎。
##段落
与员工沟通之所以令人不自在，是因为我们建立了合规与支配的体系，使沟通变得困难。我们要求人们把人性留在门外，然后用权威来改变行为。我们用人类对创造有意义工作的渴望，来掩盖企业的贪婪和短视思维。
##段落
我们如何构建以人为本的组织，同时接受这样一个事实：我们三分之二的管理者（想必薪酬优厚、训练有素、对我们的成功不可或缺）对工作中一个 essential 的部分如此不自在，以至于他们向一个陌生人坦承了这一点？
##段落
在最近的一项调查中，管理学研究生入学委员会报告称，尽管MBA在分析能力、定量专业知识和信息收集能力方面表现强劲，但他们在雇主同样看重的其他关键领域严重欠缺：战略思维、书面和口头沟通、领导力以及适应能力。这些是互斥的吗？我们必须牺牲一个来换取另一个吗？
##段落
所有真实技能的基础是这一个：彼此交谈的信心和许可。不是为了管理、贬低、恐吓或控制。而仅仅是为了寻求被理解，并付出努力去理解。
##段落
摘自塞斯·戈丁的《意义之歌：团队新宣言》，经Portfolio（企鹅出版集团旗下品牌，企鹅兰登书屋的一个部门）授权。

readings.title: 'Brutal' toll of war on Dubai's tourist trade
body: 2 April 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Sameer Hashmi Last year Dubai welcomed 19.59 million international visitors, making it one of the most-visited cities globally, but the US-Israel war with Iran has had a devastating impact on visitor numbers, and local businesses are struggling. On most evenings, Dubai's restaurants would usually be packed, with the constant buzz of diners, of tourists and residents filling tables across the city. But over the past month, many of those tables have sat empty. For Natasha Sideris, the shift has been sudden and stark. She opened her first restaurant in Dubai in 2014. Over the past decade, her Tashas hospitality group has grown to 14 outlets across the country, employing more than 1,000 people. But the US-Israel war with Iran is now taking a heavy toll on her business. Sideris says many of her restaurants, which are popular with both residents and expats, have seen revenues fall by more than 50%. But outlets that depend heavily on tourists have been hit much harder, with declines of 70% to 80%. The crisis has forced her to cut salaries by 30% for all staff including herself. "The current situation is brutal," she says. "I had a choice – either fire 30% of my staff or cut salaries to save jobs. I chose the latter for now." Sideris adds that the impact would have been worse if many of her outlets were not located inside community malls and close to residential neighbourhoods, where they still rely on local customers. The current tough reality is playing out across much of Dubai's restaurant sector. One senior executive at a restaurant chain, who asked not to be named, said footfall at its outlets has dropped to just 15-20% of normal, forcing them to place more than half of staff on unpaid leave. "We have no option," he says. "We've already shut down a few outlets temporarily, and the rest are operating with minimal staff." The impact is not limited to restaurants. The entire tourism ecosystem – from hotels and travel agencies, to transport companies and airlines – is feeling the strain. Over the past two decades, Dubai has built itself into one of the world's leading tourism hubs. Last year, the emirate welcomed 19.59 million international visitors, making it one of the most-visited cities globally. But since the war began, that momentum has been sharply disrupted. The wider UAE has come under repeated attacks, with Dubai among the key targets of Iran's military response following US and Israeli strikes. Authorities say more than 2,400 missiles and drones have been launched towards the UAE, targeting airports, ports and civilian areas, including hotels and residential buildings. More than 90% of them were intercepted and destroyed, officials say. But some debris has fallen across parts of Dubai, including major residential areas, hotels and the airport. Images of fragments striking the Fairmont hotel on the upscale Palm Island were circulated widely online. To date, 11 people have been killed and more than 185 injured across the UAE, according to authorities in the country. The conflict, which began on 28 February, has disrupted air travel across the region. In the early weeks, tens of thousands of visitors were stranded before being evacuated on special flights. Thousands of regular, scheduled flights have been cancelled since the conflict began, bringing one of the region's busiest travel hubs to a halt at times. Dubai International Airport – the world's busiest for international passengers – handled 95.2 million travellers last year.  Some operations have since resumed, with flag-carrier Emirates operating a reduced flight schedule while working to restore full network operations. But with tourists leaving and the number of new arrivals collapsing, hotel stays in Dubai have fallen steeply. Occupancy levels across Dubai hotels dropped to between 15% and 20% of the usual level for this time of the year in the weeks following the outbreak of the war, according to Mamoun Hmiden, chief business officer at travel booking firm Wego. Hotels have responded with deep discounts, particularly during the Eid period, in an attempt to attract residents. Some luxury properties on Palm Jumeirah, one of the city's premium hotel hubs, have cut prices by as much as half. "The uncertainty is disrupting everyone at the moment," says Hmiden. Some hospitality chains have temporarily shut down some properties or closed certain sections, citing scheduled renovations – a move typically seen during the quieter summer months. A senior executive at an international hospitality group said occupancy at some properties had fallen to single digits. "It made sense to cut operational costs by shutting down for a few weeks and reviewing the situation later," he says. Even business hotels are under pressure. Dubai, a major hub for conferences and events, has seen organisers cancel or postpone large gatherings in the coming months. Majestic Hotels, which operates around 450 rooms across three properties, says occupancy has dropped to record lows. "We are seeing cancellations beyond April," says Varun Raj, cluster director of sales and marketing. "A lot of events have been cancelled, making it difficult for travellers to plan ahead." The slowdown comes after several years of rapid growth. During the Covid-19 pandemic, Dubai was among the first destinations to reopen to international visitors, allowing its tourism sector to recover faster than many global peers. Since then, it has expanded into a broader and more diversified market – strengthening its position as a luxury destination, while also attracting large numbers of mid-market and price-sensitive travellers from regions such as South Asia, Europe and the former Soviet states. That surge in demand has been matched by a sharp increase in supply. Years of growth have driven expansion not only in hotel capacity, but also in short-term apartment rentals across the city. That additional supply is now under pressure. Data firm AirDNA shared that a little over 226,500 short-term bookings were cancelled across the UAE between February 28 to March 29, the first month since the war began.   The downturn is also being felt by the migrant workforce that form the backbone of Dubai's hospitality industry – from restaurant staff to hotel workers.  As demand weakens, many have seen their hours reduced, or they have been placed on unpaid leave. While the UAE's labour system allows companies to adjust quickly to changing conditions, that flexibility can leave workers exposed to sudden income losses. "It feels like we are back to the Covid-19 period," says a South Asian waiter working at a high-end restaurant. There are fears we could lose our jobs again and be forced to go back home." He and several colleagues have been placed on unpaid leave, with no clarity on when – or if – they will return to work. Some hotels, including five-star properties, have started laying off employees. Rights groups say many migrant workers in the UAE are already financially vulnerable, with some carrying debt linked to recruitment fees. The impact of the war is also being felt across the wider Middle East. Research by Tourism Economics, part of Oxford Economics, suggests that between 23 million and 38 million fewer people could travel to the region this year, depending on how long the conflict continues. Between $34bn (£25bn) and $56bn in visitor spending could be lost. "If the war ends soon, there could be a quick recovery," says Hmiden. "But if it drags on, we have to start questioning the entire summer season." This week – Dubai announced $272.26 million in support for businesses, including tourism, over the next three to six months. Hotels will be allowed to delay sales-related fees and tourism dirham charges – a fee applied to guests staying in the city.  Authorities in Dubai are also working on plans to revive tourism once the conflict subsides, including new campaigns and promotional offers.  "The war is out of our control," says one official. "But we are preparing for when it ends." More like this: • How the Iran war is affecting global travel • How a prolonged Middle East conflict could reshape how we fly • Is Dubai's glossy image under threat? Sideris is hoping that landlords will provide rent relief in the form of deferred payments or reduced payments for the time being to support local businesses. For Sideris, the outlook remains uncertain. She says a recovery is possible from October if the war ends soon. But if the conflict continues, the timeline could shift to next year – bringing the risk of layoffs and outlet closures. "We've got enough cash to see us through a month or two... maximum three, and then past that, what do we do? After that, we will have to take tougher calls. Hopefully not. And this insanity ends soon." -- For global insights and expert analysis for the boardroom and beyond, sign up to the  World of Business newsletter , while  The Essential List  delivers a handpicked selection of features and insights. ##段落
2026年4月2日 分享 保存 在Google上添加为首选 Sameer Hashmi 去年，迪拜接待了1959万国际游客，使其成为全球访问量最大的城市之一，但美国-以色列与伊朗的战争对游客数量造成了毁灭性影响，当地企业正在苦苦挣扎。大多数夜晚，迪拜的餐厅通常座无虚席，食客的嘈杂声不断，游客和居民填满了全城的餐桌。但在过去一个月里，许多餐桌空空如也。对于Natasha Sideris来说，这种转变既突然又残酷。她于2014年在迪拜开设了第一家餐厅。在过去十年中，她的Tashas酒店集团已发展到在全国拥有14家门店，雇用超过1000名员工。但美国-以色列与伊朗的战争如今正对她的生意造成沉重打击。Sideris表示，她旗下许多深受居民和外籍人士欢迎的餐厅，收入已下降超过50%。但那些严重依赖游客的门店受到的打击更为严重，降幅达70%至80%。这场危机迫使她将所有员工包括她自己的薪资削减了30%。"目前的情况非常残酷，"她说。"我有一个选择——要么裁掉30%的员工，要么削减薪资以保住工作岗位。我目前选择了后者。"Sideris补充说，如果她的许多门店不是位于社区商场内、靠近住宅区，仍然依赖本地顾客，影响会更糟。当前严峻的现实正在迪拜大部分餐饮行业中上演。一家连锁餐厅的一位要求匿名的高级高管表示，其门店的客流量已降至正常水平的15%至20%，迫使他们让超过一半的员工无薪休假。"我们别无选择，"他说。"我们已经暂时关闭了几家门店，其余的也在以最低限度的员工运营。"影响不仅限于餐厅。整个旅游生态系统——从酒店和旅行社，到运输公司和航空公司——都感受到了压力。在过去二十年中，迪拜已将自身打造为世界领先的旅游中心之一。去年，该酋长国接待了1959万国际游客，使其成为全球访问量最大的城市之一。但自战争开始以来，这一势头被急剧打断。更广泛的阿联酋多次遭到袭击，迪拜是美国和以色列打击后伊朗军事反应的主要目标之一。当局表示，已有超过2400枚导弹和无人机射向阿联酋，目标是机场、港口和民用区域，包括酒店和住宅楼。官员称，其中超过90%被拦截并摧毁。但一些碎片落在了迪拜的部分地区，包括

##段落
主要住宅区、酒店和机场。碎片击中高档棕榈岛费尔蒙酒店的画面在网上广泛传播。据阿联酋当局称，迄今为止，全国已有11人死亡、185余人受伤。这场冲突始于2月28日，已扰乱整个地区的航空旅行。最初几周，数万名旅客滞留，后被特别航班疏散。自冲突爆发以来，数千架定期航班被取消，使该地区最繁忙的旅行枢纽之一时而陷入停摆。迪拜国际机场——全球国际旅客吞吐量最大的机场——去年接待了9520万人次旅客。此后部分运营已恢复，旗舰航空公司阿联酋航空以缩减的航班时刻表运营，同时努力恢复全线网络运营。但随着游客离开、新入境人数骤降，迪拜的酒店入住率大幅下滑。据旅行预订公司Wego首席商务官Mamoun Hmiden称，战争爆发后的数周内，迪拜各地酒店的入住率降至往年同期正常水平的15%至20%。酒店纷纷推出大幅折扣，尤其是在开斋节期间，以试图吸引本地居民入住。棕榈朱美拉——该市高端酒店聚集地之一——的一些豪华酒店已将价格下调多达一半。“当前的不确定性让所有人都受到冲击，”Hmiden说。一些酒店集团已暂时关闭部分物业或关闭某些区域，理由是计划中的翻新——这种做法通常出现在较为清闲的夏季月份。一家国际酒店集团的高管表示，部分物业的入住率已降至个位数。“关闭几周以削减运营成本、日后再评估形势，是合理的做法，”他说。就连商务酒店也承受着压力。迪拜作为会议和活动的重要枢纽，已有组织者取消或推迟未来数月的大型聚会。Majestic Hotels在三个物业中运营约450间客房，称入住率已降至历史低点。“我们看到4月之后的预订也在取消，”集群销售与营销总监Varun Raj说。“大量活动被取消，使旅客难以提前规划。”这一放缓出现在数年快速增长之后。新冠疫情期间，迪拜是最早向国际游客重新开放的目的地之一，使其旅游业比许多全球同行恢复得更快。此后，它已扩展为更广泛、更多元化的市场——巩固了其作为豪华目的地的地位，同时

##段落
这也吸引了大量来自南亚、欧洲和前苏联国家等地区的中端市场和价格敏感型旅客。需求的激增与供应的急剧增加相匹配。多年的增长不仅推动了酒店容量的扩张，也带动了全市短租公寓的发展。这些新增供应如今正面临压力。数据公司AirDNA分享称，在2月28日至3月29日期间——即战争开始后的第一个月——阿联酋全国有略超22.65万笔短租预订被取消。作为迪拜酒店业支柱的外来务工群体——从餐厅员工到酒店工作人员——也感受到了经济低迷的冲击。随着需求减弱，许多人工作时间被削减，或被安排无薪休假。虽然阿联酋的劳动制度允许企业根据情况变化快速调整，但这种灵活性可能使工人面临收入骤减的风险。“感觉就像回到了新冠疫情时期，”一位在高档餐厅工作的南亚服务员说。“我们担心可能再次失去工作，被迫回国。”他和几位同事已被安排无薪休假，何时——甚至能否——重返工作岗位尚不明朗。包括五星级酒店在内的一些酒店已开始裁员。人权组织表示，阿联酋的许多外来务工者本就经济脆弱，部分人还背负着与招聘费用相关的债务。战争的影响也波及整个中东地区。牛津经济研究院旗下旅游经济学部门的研究表明，根据冲突持续时间的不同，今年前往该地区的旅客人数可能减少2300万至3800万。游客消费损失可能在340亿至560亿美元之间。“如果战争很快结束，可能会迅速复苏，”赫米登说。“但如果拖下去，我们就不得不开始质疑整个夏季旅游季了。”本周，迪拜宣布在未来三到六个月内提供2.7226亿美元的企业支持，涵盖旅游业。酒店将被允许推迟缴纳与销售相关的费用和旅游迪拉姆费——一项针对在该市入住旅客征收的费用。迪拜当局还在制定冲突平息后重振旅游业的计划，包括新的推广活动和促销优惠。“战争是我们无法控制的，”一位官员说。“但我们正在为战争结束做准备。”更多相关内容：• 伊朗战争如何影响全球旅行 • 中东冲突持续可能如何重塑我们的出行方式 • 迪拜的光鲜形象是否受到威胁？西德里斯希望房东能通过延期付款或暂时减租的方式提供租金减免，以支持本地企业。对于Si

##段落
德里斯的说法是，前景仍不明朗。她表示，如果战争很快结束，十月起有望复苏。但如果冲突持续，时间线可能推迟到明年——届时将面临裁员和门店关闭的风险。“我们的现金够撑一两个月……最多三个月，再往后怎么办？到那时，我们就不得不做出更艰难的决定。希望不会走到那一步。也希望这场疯狂能早日结束。”——欲获取面向董事会及更广泛决策层的全球洞察与专家分析，请订阅《商业世界》通讯，而《必读清单》则精选特稿与洞察。欲了解更多商业及更多领域内容，请在领英上关注我们。商业 战争 新闻 特稿 伊朗战争 商业世界

readings.title: Why a global outbreak of plague is unlikely
body: 14 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Jasmin Fox-Skelly A Russian lab technician has died at a plague research centre in Siberia, but there are many reasons pneumonic plague is usually easily contained. It may seem eerily familiar. On Friday last week, a woman died from pneumonia of "undetermined" origin in Siberia after potentially being exposed to the plague. Russian media have reported that nearly 200 people were placed in isolation. Officials quickly shut down concern, but online speculation and alarm have been spreading.  The 28-year-old woman, named Darya Shipilova, worked at the Anti-Plague Institute in Siberia's Irkutsk region. Unconfirmed reports suggested the woman fell ill with pneumonia-like symptoms either after breaking a test tube containing the plague bacterium, or following a field trip to the Buryatia region on the border with Mongolia. In this area, plague is endemic among wild animals.  As of this date no cause of death has been officially confirmed for Shipilova and laboratory testing is reportedly underway. But one thing is clear. Experts say that the case is unlikely to lead to a global outbreak. Here's why. The plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis . Clinically there are three forms : bubonic plague, pneumonic plague and septicaemic plague. The bubonic plague is the most common variant and is spread by the bites of infected fleas. Once inside a human host, the bacterium travels to the lymph nodes where it causes painful sores called 'buboes' in the groin, neck and armpits. Human-to-human transmission of bubonic plague is rare, but the bacterium can spread to the blood where it causes septicaemic plague, or the lungs, causing pneumonic plague. Unlike the other forms of plague, the pneumonic version can pass from person to person via tiny droplets released into the air when a person coughs or sneezes. Pneumonic plague is also usually fatal unless treated early, and the time from exposure to when symptoms begin can be as short as 24 hours. The Black Death, caused by bubonic and pneumonic plague, killed more than 25 million people in Europe in the 14th Century, wiping out between one third to two thirds of the population. It was made possible by newly opened trade routes , and the importing of goods such as grain and flour via ships. However, modern conditions are much less hospitable for the spread of the plague.  Firstly, while the pneumonic version of Yersinia pestis is nearly always fatal if left untreated, today it can be overcome with simple, widely available antibiotics.  "We have two treatments that work very well for bubonic plague," says Piero Olliaro, professor of poverty-related infectious diseases at the University of Oxford. The bioterrorism threat Health authorities including the US Center for Disease Control and Prevention have plans for how to respond if the plague is released intentionally. This includes tracing contacts, providing guidance to hospitals, and sourcing medical supplies. The risk is considered low, but the plague has been used as a weapon before . Anecdotal reports suggest infected corpses were thrown at enemies in the 14th Century, and the Japanese military dropped infected fleas on Chinese civilians during World War Two.  In 2025, Olliaro and colleagues published the first ever randomised, controlled trial for the treatment of bubonic plague in Madagascar. It showed that two antibiotics – oral ciprofloxacin and injectable aminoglycoside – were 91% and 92% effective at treating bubonic plague, respectively. Even in the handful of cases where a person's plague became pneumonic, 85% of people got better and survived with swift treatment.  Another reason that a plague pandemic is very unlikely is that, unlike the Covid-19 virus, pneumonic plague can only be spread after symptoms begin. This is usually within 24 hours. Symptoms are severe and obvious. This means that any further cases can be quickly identified, isolated and treated before transmission occurs. "It's not something that we can miss, where we would see people getting on a plane and travelling around and seeing new infections everywhere ," says Zania Stamataki, associate professor of viral immunology at the University of Birmingham. It would be quite obvious, quite quickly, she says.  According to the World Health Organisation , all the patients' contacts have reportedly been identified and are being monitored, with none showing symptoms of illness currently. This action is in line with public health advice given by the US Center for Disease Control, which recommends identifying persons considered at risk so that they can be monitored, screened, quarantined and given antibiotics. Christian Lindmeier, spokesperson for the World Health Organisation, announced the organisation's initial risk assessment on Tuesday. It's "moderate to low for Irkutsk, a low risk for the Russian Federation as a whole and very low for the WHO European region", he told reporters.  Generally speaking, transmission in a laboratory environment is an extremely rare event, as rigorous protocols are usually in place to prevent accidental exposure. "These are very specialised labs," says Stamataki. "There are layers and layers of protection." For instance, Stamataki explains that researchers wear full personal protection equipment (PPE). Samples are also only handled within biosafety cabinets. These safety cabinets are under negative air pressure, which means that the flow of air goes inwards and away from the user. "If a tube breaks, it would break inside the cabinet, and the user would be protected," she says.  Even when you are transporting a tube, the tube is housed in a secondary containment vessel, explains Stamataki. Technicians also undergo vigorous training before working in such laboratories, she says. One of the main reasons that plague spread so rapidly in the 14th Century is the generally poor living conditions at that time. Waste and food scraps littered the streets , creating ideal nesting grounds for the black rats that carried the disease-bearing fleas. People lived in very close proximity to one another, and traders spent months in cramped ships. These conditions no longer exist for much of the world. More like this: •   How bubonic plague rewired the human immune system •  Leprosy: The ancient disease scientists can't solve •  A genetic quirk protects us from norovirus. Can vaccines help the rest of us? Nevertheless, it's important to state that the plague isn't just a historical disease. Plague is endemic in rodent populations in Africa, Asia, South America and even the US . Every year there are cases in humans too. In the US, for example, an average of seven human plague cases are reported each year. In some parts of the world, there are also sometimes local outbreaks where human to human transmission of pneumonic plague occurs. In 2017, an outbreak in Madagascar led to 2,417 cases of the plague and 209 deaths. However, Olliaro points out that the fact that this ended is evidence that plague outbreaks tend to be confined. They don't usually lead to a pandemic.  However, while an outbreak of the plague is unlikely to achieve truly global spread, this doesn't mean that we shouldn't invest in treating and preventing plague. "It may not impact many people on the global scale, but it still causes suffering," says Olliaro. "It is an important disease, and so we should not forget that plague exists." -- For trusted insights on health and wellbeing, sign up to the Health Fix newsletter by senior health correspondent Melissa Hogenboom who also writes the Live Well For Longer and Six Steps to Calm courses.   For more science, technology, environment and health stories from the BBC, follow us on Facebook and Instagram .  Health Outbreak Pandemic Infectious disease Science Features

##段落
14小时前 分享 保存 在Google上添加为首选 Jasmin Fox-Skelly 一名俄罗斯实验室技术员在西伯利亚的一家鼠疫研究中心死亡，但肺鼠疫通常容易被控制的原因有很多。这看起来可能似曾相识。上周五，一名女子在西伯利亚死于“未确定”来源的肺炎，此前她可能接触过鼠疫。俄罗斯媒体报道称，近200人被隔离。官员迅速平息了担忧，但网络上的猜测和恐慌一直在蔓延。

##段落
这名28岁女子名叫达里娅·希皮洛娃，在西伯利亚伊尔库茨克地区的抗鼠疫研究所工作。未经证实的报道称，这名女子可能是在打破一支装有鼠疫杆菌的试管后，或是在前往与蒙古接壤的布里亚特地区进行实地考察后，出现了类似肺炎的症状。在该地区，鼠疫在野生动物中呈地方性流行。

##段落
截至这一天，希皮洛娃的死因尚未得到官方确认，据报道实验室检测正在进行中。但有一件事是明确的。专家表示，此病例不太可能引发全球疫情。原因如下。鼠疫由鼠疫耶尔森菌引起。临床上共有三种形式：腺鼠疫、肺鼠疫和败血型鼠疫。腺鼠疫是最常见的变种，通过受感染跳蚤的叮咬传播。一旦进入人体宿主，这种细菌会前往淋巴结，并在腹股沟、颈部和腋下引起被称为“腹股沟淋巴结炎”的疼痛性溃疡。腺鼠疫的人际传播很少见，但该细菌可以扩散到血液中，引起败血型鼠疫，或扩散到肺部，引起肺鼠疫。与其他形式的鼠疫不同，肺鼠疫可以通过人咳嗽或打喷嚏时释放到空气中的微小飞沫在人与人之间传播。肺鼠疫通常也是致命的，除非及早治疗，而从暴露到症状开始的时间可能短至24小时。

##段落
由腺鼠疫和肺鼠疫引起的黑死病在14世纪导致欧洲超过2500万人死亡，消灭了三分之一到三分之二的人口。新开辟的贸易路线，以及通过船只进口谷物和面粉等货物，使这一切成为可能。然而，现代条件对鼠疫传播要不利得多。首先，虽然鼠疫耶尔森菌的肺鼠疫型如果不治疗几乎总是致命，但如今可以通过简单、广泛可得的抗生素治愈。“我们有两种对腺鼠疫非常有效的治疗方法，”牛津大学贫困相关传染病教授皮耶罗·奥利亚罗说。生物恐怖主义威胁 包括美国中心在内的卫生当局

##段落
美国疾病控制与预防中心已制定计划，以应对鼠疫被蓄意释放的情况。这些计划包括追踪接触者、为医院提供指导以及采购医疗物资。目前风险被认为较低，但鼠疫此前曾被用作武器。有零星报道称，14世纪曾有人将感染鼠疫的尸体抛向敌人，二战期间日军也曾向中国平民投放感染鼠疫的跳蚤。2025年，Olliaro及其同事发表了全球首个针对马达加斯加腺鼠疫治疗的随机对照试验。结果显示，两种抗生素——口服环丙沙星和注射用氨基糖苷类——治疗腺鼠疫的有效率分别为91%和92%。即使在少数患者病情发展为肺鼠疫的情况下，85%的人在及时治疗后康复并存活。鼠疫大流行极不可能的另一个原因是，与新冠病毒不同，肺鼠疫只有在症状出现后才会传播。这通常在24小时内发生。症状严重且明显。这意味着任何后续病例都能在传播发生前被迅速识别、隔离和治疗。伯明翰大学病毒免疫学副教授Zania Stamataki表示：“这不是那种我们会漏掉的事情——不会出现患者登上飞机四处旅行、到处出现新感染的情况。”她说，情况会相当明显，而且相当迅速。据世界卫生组织称，所有患者的接触者据报道均已找到并正在接受监测，目前无人出现疾病症状。此举符合美国疾病控制中心发布的公共卫生建议，该建议推荐识别被认为有风险的人员，以便对其进行监测、筛查、隔离并给予抗生素。世界卫生组织发言人Christian Lindmeier于周二宣布了该组织的初步风险评估。他告诉记者，对于伊尔库茨克而言风险为“中到低”，对整个俄罗斯联邦而言风险为低，对世卫组织欧洲区域而言风险极低。

##段落
一般来说，实验室环境中的传播是极为罕见的事件，因为通常有严格的规程来防止意外暴露。“这些都是非常专业的实验室，”Stamataki说。“有层层叠叠的防护。”例如，Stamataki解释说，研究人员会穿戴全套个人防护装备（PPE）。样本也仅在生物安全柜内处理。这些安全柜处于负压状态，意味着气流向内流动，远离使用者。“如果试管破裂，它会在柜内破裂，使用者会……”

readings.title: Will Trump’s diesel order do anything?
body: Politics / Donald Trump / The Logoff Will Trump’s diesel order do anything? ﻿Why red-dye diesel probably isn’t the fix the White House needs. by Cameron Peters Oct 6, 2026, 10:00 PM UTC Gift Donald Trump holds up a signed executive order on diesel access at a rally in in Grand Island, Nebraska, on October 5, 2026. Win McNamee/Getty Images Cameron Peters is a staff editor at Vox. This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here . Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump is trying to fix the diesel crisis he caused. What’s happening? On Monday evening, Trump signed an executive order intended to lower diesel prices by temporarily expanding access to red-dye diesel. What’s red-dye diesel? A kind of diesel usually reserved for farm and construction equipment and other off-road uses — and marked with a little bit of red dye to distinguish it from other diesel sold for use in on-road vehicles. Ordinarily, it’s tax-exempt and not available to on-road vehicles, but Trump is expanding access in a bid to bring down the overall cost of fuel ahead of the midterm elections. Trump’s order defers payment on — but does not actually suspend — the federal tax on red-dye diesel for on-road vehicles through the end of the year, while also directing his Cabinet “to explore pathways to eliminate the obligation to pay the deferred taxes.” What’s the context? Diesel prices are way, way up because of the Iran war. Currently, the national average price per gallon is $6.32, compared to $3.68/gallon one year ago. Will this do anything to lower prices? Not very much, in all likelihood, for a whole slew of reasons ably explained here — including that the order can’t change the underlying reality of a global diesel shortage. Why does the price of diesel matter? Most people don’t use diesel to fill up their tank, but semitrucks shipping food and other goods around the country rely on it. That means that when diesel gets more expensive, nearly everything else does too , sooner or later. The hidden $350 surcharge on American households Why does Trump care? This is best explained by the fact that Trump signed the executive order while on the campaign trail in Nebraska — ordinarily a comfortably Republican state that instead looks potentially in play for independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn. High diesel prices have hit hard in Nebraska and other agriculture-heavy states like Iowa and Kansas, jeopardizing Republican Senate seats in all three. 欢迎来到The Logoff：唐纳德·特朗普正试图修复他自己造成的柴油危机。发生了什么？周一晚间，特朗普签署了一项行政令，意图通过临时扩大红色柴油的供应渠道来降低柴油价格。什么是红色柴油？这是一种通常保留给农用和建筑设备及其他非道路用途的柴油——通过添加少量红色染料来区别于供道路车辆使用的其他柴油。通常情况下，它享受免税待遇，且不供道路车辆使用，但特朗普正在扩大其供应渠道，以期在中期选举前压低整体燃料成本。特朗普的行政令将道路车辆使用红色柴油的联邦税推迟缴纳——但并未真正暂停征收——直至年底，同时指示其内阁“探索消除缴纳递延税款义务的途径”。背景是什么？由于伊朗战争，柴油价格已大幅飙升。目前全国平均价格为每加仑6.32美元，而一年前为每加仑3.68美元。这能起到降低价格的作用吗？很可能作用非常有限，原因众多，此处已有详尽解释——包括该行政令无法改变全球柴油短缺这一根本现实。为什么柴油价格重要？大多数人不用柴油给自己的车加油，但在全国运输食品和其他货物的半挂卡车依赖柴油。这意味着当柴油涨价时，几乎所有其他东西迟早也会跟着涨。美国家庭隐藏的350美元附加费 特朗普为什么在意？最好的解释是，特朗普是在内布拉斯加州竞选途中签署这项行政令的——该州通常是共和党的稳赢州，但如今看来可能对独立参议员候选人丹·奥斯本构成竞争。高柴油价格对内布拉斯加州以及艾奥瓦州和堪萨斯州等其他农业重州造成了严重打击，危及这三个州的共和党参议院席位。邮箱（必填） 注册 提交您的邮箱即表示您同意我们的条款和隐私声明。本网站受reCAPTCHA保护，适用谷歌隐私政策和服务条款。这里有一篇值得点击的故事

readings.title: Feeling unseen by your boss? Here’s what you can do
body: Feeling unseen by your boss? Here’s what you can do

Ever have your hard work — including your successes — go unnoticed by your manager? Fixable , TED’s new podcast, is here to do just that — to fix the problems of everyday people who call in with their work woes.

In episode four , cohosts and top leadership coaches Frances Frei and Anne Morriss got to know Nai’a, a caller who struggled with receiving recognition after a major reorganization paired her with a new and preoccupied boss. Nai’a was going above and beyond to do her job well, but the lack of acknowledgement and encouragement — and even awareness — of her work was causing her to lose motivation.
Frances’s and Anne’s first piece of advice to Nai’a was simple: See the humanness of what’s going on — and of your manager.

“Sometimes the barrier to showing up as a great collaborator with your manager can be that there’s still some residual frustration about the situation,” Anne explained. “But that emotion is not going to be useful to you.”
Instead, they encouraged Nai’a to recognize the humanity of her manager and forgive them for making mistakes.
Frances and Anne also shared this strategy with her to practice: Choose curiosity over judgment.

Here’s how Frances put it: “You have a choice between judgment and curiosity, because both can’t exist at the same time. So if you have judgment about your manager, you can’t really be curious about their situation. And when you’re thinking of your manager as a person who’s got a lot of part-time jobs, how do we set them up for success?”

“The simplest expression of curiosity — which is truly a magical elixir in a workplace — is in the form of questions,” said Anne. For example, you could start by asking your manager what process works best for them to learn about your accomplishments and contributions. Or, you could focus on how you can make your meetings with them more productive by asking them, “How can our one-on-one time be of service to what we’re trying to achieve together?”

Another option: Be open about your concerns, and ask your manager what their vision of your success looks like. You could say something like, “Here’s my fear: I’m working really hard, and in this state of flux, I’m afraid that six months will go by and people are going to wonder whether or not I did a good job. So it’s just helpful for me to be clear — what is a good job and how can I help in getting that data for you?”

Across industries and across the world, many people are going through workplace reorganizations and other sweeping changes. And like Nai’a, it’s normal to feel anxious and stressed by what’s happening and to need to go through a readjustment period. Leading with questions — and seeing your boss as another human you’re collaborating with — can help you gain back some agency and autonomy.

“Try doing what you can, and marvel at how the other person changes as a result, as opposed to coming up with the list of how you would like the other person to change,” said Frances. “I think you’re going to be pleasantly surprised; that’s the beautiful part of this.”

No matter your job or business, you’ll find actionable advice on Fixable that can improve your workdays. In other episodes, learn how to overcome communication roadblocks, scale up your side project and lead more productive meetings. Plus: Click here for a chance to get your own work question answered on the show! Listen to Fixable now wherever you get your podcasts.
About the author Hayley Caldwell is a copywriter on the Audience Development team at TED.

你有没有经历过自己的辛勤付出——包括那些亮眼的成绩——却被上司忽视？TED的新播客《可修复》正是为此而生——专门解决那些打电话来倾诉职场烦恼的普通人的问题。

##段落
在第四集中，联合主持人兼顶尖领导力教练弗朗西斯·弗雷和安妮·莫里斯认识了一位叫奈娅的来电者。奈娅在一次大规模重组后换了一位新上司，而这位上司又事务繁忙，她因此很难获得认可。奈娅一直在超额完成工作，但缺乏认可和鼓励——甚至上司根本不知道她做了什么——这让她逐渐失去了动力。

##段落
弗朗西斯和安妮给奈娅的第一条建议很简单：看到事情中的人性——也看到你上司的人性。

##段落
“有时候，阻碍你与上司成为优秀合作伙伴的，可能是你对现状仍有一些残留的挫败感，”安妮解释道。“但这种情绪对你没有任何帮助。”

##段落
相反，她们鼓励奈娅去认识上司作为普通人的一面，并原谅他们犯下的错误。

##段落
弗朗西斯和安妮还分享了一个可以练习的策略：选择好奇，而非评判。

##段落
弗朗西斯是这样说的：“你可以在评判和好奇之间做选择，因为两者无法同时存在。所以如果你对上司抱有评判，你就无法真正对他们的处境感到好奇。当你把上司看作一个身兼多职的人时，我们该如何帮助他们走向成功？”

##段落
“好奇最简单的表达方式——这在工作场所中真的是一剂神奇的灵药——就是以提问的形式呈现，”安妮说。比如，你可以先问上司，什么方式最方便他们了解你的成绩和贡献。或者，你可以聚焦于如何让你们之间的会议更高效，问他们：“我们的一对一时间怎样才能真正服务于我们共同想要达成的目标？”

##段落
另一个选择：坦诚地说出你的担忧，问上司他们眼中你的成功是什么样的。你可以这样说：“我的担忧是这样的：我非常努力地工作，但在这种变动的状态下，我怕六个月过去了，大家会怀疑我到底做得好不好。所以对我来说，明确一点会很有帮助——什么才算做得好，我怎样才能帮你获取这些信息？”

##段落
在各个行业、世界各地，许多人都正在经历职场重组和其他大规模变革。和奈娅一样，对正在发生的事情感到焦虑和压力、需要一段重新适应的时期，都是正常的。领导

##段落
带着问题去沟通——把老板也看作与你协作的另一个普通人——能帮你找回一些主动权和自主性。

##段落
“试着去做你力所能及的事，然后惊叹于对方因此发生的变化，而不是列出一张你希望对方如何改变的清单，”弗朗西斯说。“我想你会惊喜地发现，这正是这件事美妙的地方。”

##段落
无论你从事什么工作或行业，你都能在《Fixable》中找到可付诸实践的建议，让你的工作日变得更好。在其他几期节目中，你还能学到如何克服沟通障碍、如何扩展你的副业，以及如何主持更高效的会议。此外：点击这里，有机会让你的工作问题在节目中得到解答！现在就在你收听播客的任何平台上收听《Fixable》。
